title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Credits usage report for pay-as-you-go in Copilot Chat
summary: Hold: the report's no-cost and included-licensing assertions lack explicit support, and the automation examples are incomplete. Correct the concealment request body, replace the Cost Management namespace with an actual reporting request, and link the consumption navigation to the page that documents it.

claims.claim: The report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: The report is on by default.
claims.quote: This new report will be on by default and will be available in the Microsoft admin center at Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption:
claims.fix: Retain defaultState on and cite MC1069563 at https://admin.microsoft.com/Adminportal/Home#/MessageCenter/:/messages/MC1069563. Attribute the default and automatic rollout to that notice; distinguish its older Message consumption label from Learn's current Credits label.

claims.claim: The report appears after Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go setup in either admin center.
claims.quote: After you set up pay-as-you-go for Microsoft Copilot Chat, either in the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Power Platform admin center, and enable agent usage in your organization, you see a new report that includes metrics for credits used.
claims.fix: Include the full prerequisite in licensing.notes and Scope: after setting up Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go in either admin center and enabling agent usage, the report appears.

claims.claim: The report is included and requires no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "free" "license" cost; "Copilot Credits report" "no additional" "report". Opened Credits report and usage reports overview; read MC1069563. No explicit included report entitlement or blanket no-licence statement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown unless an explicit report entitlement is cited. Replace 'No licence for the report' with the narrower attributed fact that MC1069563 says a Microsoft Copilot license is not required for this pay-as-you-go scenario; retain the documented setup and report-role requirements.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: There is no cost for the report, justifying cost none.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "free" "license" cost; "Copilot Credits report" "no additional" "report". Opened Credits report and usage reports overview. Neither states a separate report price or that reporting is included at no charge.
claims.fix: Remove 'No cost for the report'. Say the report page states no separate reporting price. Set cost to low for the identified export/admin time and revise the rationale to note that report pricing is not stated, while underlying consumption is metered. The standard requires explicit inclusion evidence for cost none.

claims.claim: The report measures consumption by users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: The Credits used metric shows the total credits used from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The reported Copilot Chat interactions consume Copilot Credits through the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: The Credits used metric shows the total credits used from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter during the selected time period.

claims.claim: In the documented example, tenant graph grounding can consume 10 credits per prompt.
claims.quote: For example, an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In the documented example, generative answers add two credits, so agent design influences consumption.
claims.quote: For example, an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: The Cost Management Consumption dashboard reports usage by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote:
The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by:
- Spending policy
- User
- Group
- Agent
- Service
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending to sources. Describe this as reporting for supported services governed through spending policies, not a confirmed replacement for the dedicated Copilot Chat Credits report.

claims.claim: The Cost Management dashboard is newer and is where Microsoft is adding new reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Credits report Cost Management dashboard newer new reporting future. Opened managing-credits, monitoring-spending and Cost Management API overview. They describe capabilities and expanding service coverage, not this reporting chronology or direction.
claims.fix: Remove 'newer' and 'is where Microsoft is adding new reporting'. Replace with the documented current dashboard breakdowns and keep any future relationship with the Credits report as an open question.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management can lag usage by up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: Billed amounts are updated daily and sometimes more frequently. It can take 24 hours after usage of a service to show in Microsoft Cost Management.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/view-cost to sources for the pay-as-you-go billing delay.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management is a meter-oriented billing view rather than a per-person operational report.
claims.quote: Shows billing-oriented cost data, such as costs by subscription, service, resource, meter, or invoice period. It doesn't show the same user-level or spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-compare-dashboard-views and use its qualified comparison rather than the absolute 'shows meters, not people'. Note that the article focuses on experiences governed through Microsoft 365 usage-based billing policies.

claims.claim: This report covers metered Copilot Chat usage rather than general Copilot Studio consumption managed in Power Platform.
claims.quote: Yes. You can set up the pay-as-you-go billing policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center. If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.
claims.fix: Replace 'not Copilot Studio agents billed through the Power Platform admin center' with 'not a general report of all Copilot Studio agent consumption; Copilot Chat usage is included even when its billing policy was configured in the Power Platform admin center'. Distinguish workload scope from billing-setup location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report can expose employee identities alongside per-user consumption.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.
claims.fix: Clarify that identifiable details are hidden by default and the personal-data exposure arises when administrators reveal them. Retain the access and concealment review advice.

claims.claim: Reports Reader is authorised to view usage reports.
claims.quote: - Reports Reader

claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader is a relevant report-access role.
claims.quote: Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details).
claims.fix: Qualify both mentions: Usage Summary Reports Reader has no user details. Separate aggregate-report access from access to identifiable per-user consumption when recommending role restrictions.

claims.claim: Global Reader has usage-report read access.
claims.quote: microsoft.office365.usageReports/allEntities/allProperties/read | Read Office 365 usage reports
claims.fix: Cite this Global Reader role reference instead of implying that the usage reports overview lists the role. Do not promise detailed per-user visibility: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/reportroot-authorization limits Global Reader's delegated reports API access to tenant-level data.

claims.claim: Learn's Copilot reporting options lists AI Administrator as a role that can open the Copilot reports.
claims.quote: AI Administrator: Accesses the Copilot reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls: closing paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report is expressly a read-only surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "read-only" "makers"; "Copilot Credits report" settings configure disable access conceal names. Opened Credits report, usage reports overview and reporting options; none expressly states the blanket read-only assertion.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical product assertion with the documented functions: viewing and exporting consumption. The risk assessment can describe these reporting functions and the verified access/privacy boundaries without claiming an expressly documented read-only guarantee.

claims.claim: Makers influence cost without being able to see this report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "read-only" "makers". Opened Credits report, usage reports overview and Copilot reporting options. Access is role-based; no passage says makers cannot also hold an authorised reporting role.
claims.fix: Replace 'so makers influence cost without seeing this report' with 'so makers influence cost; makers who lack an authorised reporting role may need administrators to share consumption totals'.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Report concealment is configured at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
Select Org Settings.
4. On the Services tab, select Reports.
5. In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { displayConcealedNames } is the request for changing report concealment.
claims.fix: The endpoint exists, but replace the body with valid JSON including its required Boolean: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { "displayConcealedNames": true }. Explain true conceals and false reveals. Link the update method cited here rather than only the resource type, and flag that beta APIs are not supported for production applications.

claims.claim: The cited managing-credits page documents Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" API read-only makers new reporting Azure Cost Management 24 hours. Opened managing-credits and Monitor Copilot Credit spending. The former documents Configuration; only the latter gives the Consumption navigation.
claims.fix: Keep Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption, but change controls[2].ui.docs, its table link and source to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending. That page explicitly gives Copilot > Cost Management, then the Consumption tab.

claims.claim: /beta/copilot/costManagement (Cost Management API) is the automation call for the row's consumption breakdowns.
claims.quote: GET /copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}
claims.fix: Replace the namespace with an actual scoped operation, such as GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}, and cite this method page. State that it returns per-user consumption for exactly one completed UTC day, supports delegated work/school permissions only, is beta, and is not an equivalent for every UI breakdown or the dedicated Credits report.

claims.claim: A separate Cost Management API provides a programmatic consumption view.
